in_text_mentions: vaginal introitus due to the fusion of the labia majora. Her primary complaints included dysuria and intermittent urine leakage. The constant moisture in the vulvar region caused by dribbling urine resulted in irritation, leading to the progression of the labial adhesion to its complete form. Upon clinical examination, there was only a small opening of approximately 5 mm at the posterior fourchette, sufficient for urine to escape drop by drop. Additionally, the anterior fusion was accompanied by the partial disappearance of the clitoral hood, which is the skin covering the clitoris (Figure 1).

panels.attribution_text: Murina et al. Treatment of Prepubertal Labial Adhesions with Topical Estriol + Testosterone: A Case Report.. Pediatric reports 2024. doi:10.3390/pediatric16030047. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: Upon inspection, the labia majora were glabrous and normal for age. Moreover, the lower 2/3 of the labia minora appeared fused, causing a sub-stenosis of the vaginal introitus, and the urethral meatus was only partially visible. With gentle lateral traction of the skin, a translucent area of stickiness was evident at the point of labial fusion, leading to a diagnosis of prepubertal labial adhesion (Figure 1).

plate_findings.evidence: Labial adhesions are observed at the 0 and 6 o'clock positions at the vaginal introitus

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photograph of the vulva showing labial adhesions at the 0 and 6 o'clock positions with vaginal introitus stenosis, consistent with the configured disease labial adhesions due to vulvovaginal lichen planus. Mucosal erythema and lace-like hyperkeratosis are also present. B: H&E skin biopsy from the labia showing hyperkeratosis, atrophic epidermis, band-like chronic inflammatory infiltrate, and Civatte bodies, consistent with lichen planus, the underlying cause of the labial adhesions in this article.
panels.attribution_text: Sawada et al. Labial adhesions due to vulvovaginal lichen planus suspected to be caused by angiotensin II receptor blocker.. IJU case reports 2025. doi:10.1002/iju5.12815. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Before discontinuation of ARB. (a) Photograph of the vulva at the initial examination. Labial adhesions are observed at the 0 and 6 o'clock positions at the vaginal introitus, resulting in vaginal introitus stenosis. Mucosal erythema and lace‐like hyperkeratosis are observed mainly in the vaginal introitus. (b) Skin biopsy at the time of labia detachment showing hyperkeratosis, mildly atrophic epidermis with flattened basal keratinocytes, and a band‐like infiltrate of chronic inflammatory cells involving the subepidermal dermis. Civatte bodies are also observed in the suprabasal layers (Hematoxylin and eosin; total magnification ×100).
